name: Whale shark
size: Around 9 m at maturity; adults can grow much larger.
facts: The whale shark is the largest living fish.
It filters food such as plankton from seawater.
Its broad, flat head and pale spotted pattern make it distinctive.

name: Epaulette shark
habitat: Shallow coral reefs around northern Australia and New Guinea.
size: Adults roughly 0.6–1 m; reported maximum about 1.07 m.
facts: It can use its fins to walk along the seabed.
The large dark spot above each pectoral fin gives it its name.
It searches reef flats and tide pools for small prey.

name: Blacktip reef shark
habitat: Shallow coral reefs and sand flats in the tropical Indo-Pacific.
size: Adults roughly 1–1.6 m; some reach about 1.8 m.
facts: Its fins have striking black tips.
It often stays close to familiar reef areas.
It eats fish, crustaceans and other small sea animals.

name: Whitetip reef shark
habitat: Coral reefs and reef caves in the Indo-Pacific and eastern tropical Pacific.
size: Adults usually about 1–1.8 m; rarely larger.
facts: Its first dorsal fin and upper tail have white tips.
It often rests in reef caves during the day and hunts at night.
It can breathe while resting without swimming forward.

name: Bonnethead
habitat: Warm, shallow coastal bays and estuaries of the western Atlantic.
size: Often about 1–1.2 m as an adult; maximum about 1.5 m.
facts: Its evenly rounded head looks like a shovel.
It is a small member of the hammerhead family.
Its back teeth help crush hard prey such as crabs.

name: Leopard shark
habitat: Sandy or muddy bays and estuaries of the eastern Pacific.
size: Adults average about 1.2–1.5 m; larger individuals occur.
facts: Dark saddle-shaped marks decorate its back.
It often swims in schools, sometimes with other shark species.
It feeds on small fish and bottom-dwelling animals such as crabs.

name: Coral Comet
facts: Leaves a trail of tiny star-shaped bubbles.
Collects coral-colored pebbles in groups of five.

name: Moonfin
facts: A sleepy explorer with a glowing crescent fin.
Counts constellations before going to sleep.

name: Bubble Buddy
facts: Blows bubble rings that never quite pop.
Keeps its treasures in perfectly equal groups.

name: Sunny Saw
facts: Its pretend saw-shaped nose cuts birthday cake, not fish.
Invites every sea creature to its counting picnics.

name: Mint Mischief
facts: Hides tiny treasure maps in the kelp.
Always leaves a useful clue for a friend.

name: Star Skipper
facts: Skips across the waves like a pebble.
Loves making patterns with bright little stars.

name: Peach Pirate
facts: Shares every imaginary treasure equally.
Its pirate flag is really a very fancy napkin.

name: Cloud Cruiser
facts: Swims through clouds in its dreams.
Makes soft landing spots for tired explorers.

name: Jelly Jester
facts: Wears a hat made from a pretend jellyfish.
Knows a different silly joke for every times table.

name: Kelp Knight
facts: Protects the smallest fish with a leafy shield.
Practises brave deeds, never battles.

name: Rainbow Ripple
facts: Its fins change color with every happy thought.
Makes ripples in repeating patterns.

name: Disco Dorsal
facts: Has a glitter-ball fin and two left flippers.
Always dances in groups of eight beats.
